chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Through the intellect, the profundity of wisdom is extracted; and through wisdom, the profundity of the intellect is extracted; and through excellence in governance, righteous conduct comes about.'
He said: And he used to say: 'Reflection is the life of the discerning heart, just as the wayfarer walks in darkness with light, through excellence in extrication and the minimizing of hesitation.'

key_terms.الأدب الصالح: Righteous conduct (al-adab al-salih) — the fruit of good governance and wisdom
key_terms.البصير: The discerning one (al-basir) — one who sees with inner vision beyond mere sight
key_terms.التفكر: Reflection/contemplation (tafakkur) — sustained intellectual engagement with meaning
key_terms.الحكمة: Wisdom (hikma) — deeper practical wisdom arising from knowledge and reflection
key_terms.العقل: Intellect/reason ('aql) — the faculty of rational understanding, central to Shia epistemology
key_terms.غور: Depth/profundity (ghawr) — the hidden layers of meaning extracted through reflection

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about intellect and wisdom in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a double-aphorism attributed to Imam Ali (peace be upon him), the Commander of the Faithful, emphasizing the dynamic interplay between intellect ('aql) and wisdom (hikma): each deepens the other in a mutually enriching cycle. Good governance then yields righteous conduct. The second aphorism compares reflection (tafakkur) to a lamp carried by a wise traveler navigating darkness — the discerning heart comes alive through deep contemplation, moving swiftly and without hesitation. This teaching was likely directed at the intellectual circles of Kufa and Medina, where al-Kulayni's early scholarly community prized rational engagement with religious knowledge.
